title: Event sitemap entries declared lastmod as the start date, which is in the future for every upcoming event

source.ref: found 2026-10-05 by the scan-seven SEO/GEO finders (26-agent fan-out), confirmed by hand against the tree

detail: FOUND 2026-10-05 (scan seven, seo-sitemap finder). lib/events/series-seo.ts documented startsAt as the sitemap's lastModified, and app/sitemap.ts wrote it, so every upcoming event carried a future lastmod. Google documents a consistently inaccurate lastmod as grounds to ignore the field for the whole file, which would also cost the Space, help and journey entries their real dates. CLOSED 2026-10-05: event entries carry NO lastModified. `events` has no updated_at column (created_at only, checked on production and in lib/database.types.ts), so there is nothing true to send, and absent beats invented (LIVE-197). A first draft selected updated_at; tsc refused it, and at runtime PostgREST would have failed the read and emptied every event out of the sitemap. lib/events/series-seo.test.ts pins the absence of the start-date lastmod. A real modified stamp for events is a migration (column + trigger) and its own row if anyone wants one.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const sm=fs.readFileSync("app/sitemap.ts","utf8");const r=fs.readFileSync("lib/events/series-seo.ts","utf8");if(/lastModified: new Date\(e\.startsAt\)/.test(sm)||/updated_at/.test(r)){console.error("SCAN-661: event sitemap entries declare lastmod as the START date (future for every upcoming event, grounds for Google to ignore the field file-wide), or the reader selects an updated_at column events does not have, which fails the read and empties the events section.");process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Fails on main before this change; passes with it.
